disclaimer: All records checked against the source identification and publisher/institution abstract or official standard page. Full texts were not systematically reviewed. Findings are source-scoped; application guidance in cards is extrapolation unless explicitly noted.

claims.source_supported_summary: Four studies developed a measure and identified classical/expressive dimensions of perceived website aesthetics.
claims.source_scope: Website aesthetic rating instruments, not screen-specific CSS rules.
claims.do_not_infer: Do not assert an objective ideal style or validated 100-point custom rubric.

claims.source_supported_summary: Seven studies identified distinguishable facets of perceived aesthetics: simplicity, diversity, color, craftsmanship.
claims.do_not_infer: Do not make a fixed checklist with assumed causal improvements.
claims.selected_primary_text_support: In Study 6, 78 people evaluated alternate color designs after tasks; the color manipulation selectively affected Colorfulness (not the other facets). Study 7 compared aesthetically pleasing/distorted websites with 375 participants. These are source-specific validations of the measure, not a design recipe.

claims.source_supported_summary: Visual complexity and prototypicality affected rapid screenshot aesthetics judgments; low-complexity/high-prototypicality screens were generally preferred in these studies.
claims.source_scope: Very short first impressions from screenshots.
claims.do_not_infer: Not proof that unconventional designs always perform worse or users accomplish tasks faster.

claims.source_supported_summary: Quantitative graphical decoding accuracy varies with the elementary perceptual task.
claims.source_scope: Graph designs for accurate quantitative extraction.
claims.do_not_infer: Not a blanket prohibition on pie charts or claims about aesthetic preference.

claims.source_supported_summary: Design/validation can be distinguished into domain, abstraction, visual encoding/interaction, and algorithm layers.
claims.do_not_infer: Not validated as a mandatory sequence for all UI projects.
claims.selected_primary_text_support: The author describes four nested levels and states that designers need not always perform them in linear order. Wrong upstream abstraction can spoil even correct downstream encoding/algorithm.

claims.source_supported_summary: The methodology proposes nine stages, informed by 21 design studies and literature survey.
claims.source_scope: Domain expert collaboration and visualization design studies.
claims.do_not_infer: Not a controlled trial proving nine stages universally superior.
claims.selected_primary_text_support: Article introduction states the authors reflected on 21 prior design studies (3 assessed as failures by authors), plus literature, and proposes nine stages. This is reflective methodology, not an RCT.

claims.source_supported_summary: The information-seeking mantra is a starting point, together with data/task taxonomies.
claims.do_not_infer: Not a universal home-page wireframe or required overview panel.

claims.source_supported_summary: Visual attributes including color and recognizable objects related to visualization memorability in this study.
claims.do_not_infer: Memorability does not establish comprehension, data accuracy or task success.

claims.source_supported_summary: Protocol studies of nine experienced designers supported problem/solution co-evolution.
claims.source_scope: Industrial design tasks and protocol observations.
claims.do_not_infer: Not proof that every task needs broad problem reframing.

claims.source_supported_summary: Provided examples induced design fixation in studied conceptual design tasks.
claims.do_not_infer: Do not infer that all references harm creativity.

claims.source_supported_summary: Across 43 studies examples narrowed solution-category diversity yet improved idea novelty/quality in reported aggregate results.
claims.do_not_infer: Do not collapse diverse outcomes into examples always good/bad.

claims.source_supported_summary: Parallel prototype creation before critique outperformed serial prototyping in tested novice web advertisement design tasks.
claims.do_not_infer: No demonstrated effect here for all AI agents or high-stakes admin UIs.

claims.source_supported_summary: Review of 180 HCI studies found recurring validity limitations in the choice of usability measures.
claims.do_not_infer: A single subjective score cannot prove task performance.

claims.source_supported_summary: WCAG 2.2 AA target size of 24 CSS px has spacing, equivalent, inline, user-agent-control and essential exceptions.
claims.do_not_infer: Small controls are not automatic violations without evaluating exceptions.

claims.source_supported_summary: Non-text contrast 1.4.11 applies to visual information required for identifying components/states and meaningful graphics.
claims.do_not_infer: Not every decorative border is required to have 3:1 contrast.

claims.source_supported_summary: Focus Not Obscured minimum 2.4.11 prohibits fully hiding focused controls behind author-created content.
claims.do_not_infer: Does not require every anchor section heading to be fully visible; separately test task quality.

claims.source_supported_summary: Text Spacing 1.4.12 is an override-resilience requirement, not a requirement to author exact spacing values.
claims.do_not_infer: Do not claim a mandatory base CSS letter-spacing of 0.12em.

claims.source_supported_summary: ISO 9241-210:2019 specifies requirements and recommendations for human-centred design activities and principles throughout system lifecycle.
claims.do_not_infer: Full normative requirements were not checked, so do not claim ISO certification/compliance.
